newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets Chubais, address set for March 6.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets Chubais, address set for March 6.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin met chief-of staff Anatoly Chubais on Friday to discuss his annual address to parliament, which will probabaly take place on March 6, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said.
Yegor Stroyev, the head of the upper house of parliament, had said on Thursday that the address was likely on March 5.

"The president met the head of the Kremlin administration for about 40 minutes at the Gorky-9 residence... and discussed in detail the structure and content of his planned address," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.
Yeltsin is recovering from pneumonia at Gorky-9 outside Moscow and, on doctors' orders, only makes brief working trips to the Kremlin.
Yeltsin, who is keen to prove that he is still firmly in control of affairs despite ill health, wants the text of his address "toughened up", Yastrzhembsky said.

Asked if the president would be strong enough to deliver his full address from the podium, Yastrzhembsky said "for the time being no changes in the normal procedure and form of the address are envisaged". The speech usually lasts 30-40 minutes.

Doctors said on Wednesday that Yeltsin would need at least another 10 days to recover fully from his pneumonia, which struck just two weeks after his return to the Kremlin after recuperating from open heart surgery.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Chubais also discussed next month's planned summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helskinki and the hostage crisis in Tajikistan, where rebels are holding Russian journalists and U.N. military observers.
"The president is extremely alarmed by the situation of the hostages in Tajikistan...and expects the Tajik authorities to do everything possible to save human lives," Yastrzhembsky said.

Itar-Tass news agency, quoting Russian Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Ignatenko, said on Friday all 14 hostages were alive, contradicting earlier reports that a U.N. military observer had been shot dead.

Outlining Yeltsin's plans for the coming week, Yastrzhembsky said the president would meet Defence Minister Igor Rodionov on Monday, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday and the new U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday.
All meetings will take place in the Kremlin.

Yastrzhembsky also said Yeltsin would meet senior European Union officials in Moscow on March 3 -- a summit meeting postponed from February 4 because Yeltsin had not recovered sufficiently from pneumonia.

Yeltsin has ordered a new commission to draw up plans clearly delineating relations between Moscow and the breakaway region of Chechnya, where President Aslan Maskhadov, a former guerrilla leader, took office on Wednesday.
The commission, headed by Ivan Rybkin, secretary of the policy-making Security Council, has until March 31 to prepare the documents, Yastrzhembsky said.
